about.body: ELENEM v2.0 — a two-dimensional role-playing game in pixel art, three-quarter top-down view. The island of Elenem, year 1430. Vertical slice: one district, a cast with daily routines, three tasks, inventory, combat, day-night cycle, a debt counter and saving. All content lives in JSON files, all text in translation files, and the systems talk to each other over an event bus.
about.principleBody: Everything must have a roleplay justification. No system appears out of thin air on a keypress: every menu has a physical counterpart in the world, and John must have a reason to use it.
about.title: About
belt.empty: Nothing useful hangs at your belt.
belt.hint: Aim to choose, confirm with E
bestiary.abbey.lore: Burned in 1428 during the rising. The walls stand, the roof is gone, and the cellar is said to be intact. Said — because nobody who went in came back with a story that can be checked.
bestiary.boar.habitat: The woods beyond the walls, oak thickets. It goes straight ahead and does not turn.
bestiary.boar.lore: Vagn teaches that you must not take a boar on the shield sideways — you wait until it gores itself. Three men last year waited too briefly.
bestiary.chanterelle.lore: Orange, smelling of apricot, growing under beech. Wiera buys them by weight and says half the mushroom pickers on the island gather something that looks similar.
bestiary.chapel.lore: A small nave, an altar, and an alms box emptied twice a week. The reliquary vanished four months ago and nobody filed a written complaint.
bestiary.crow.habitat: The gallows, the abbey ruins, Lower Town roofs.
bestiary.crow.lore: The executioner says the crows at the gallows are full and lazy. He does not want to explain what they are full of.
bestiary.deer.habitat: The woodland edge at dawn, the meadows past the tannery. It runs at the first rustle.
bestiary.deer.lore: Oles pays forty-eight crowns for a whole hide. The Wild Knights' huntsmen consider deer their property and have a forty-year-old paper saying so.
bestiary.dog.habitat: The tannery, the smithy yard, the north gate. It barks at the smell of salt and blood.
bestiary.dog.lore: Oles's dog does not bite people, it only stops them. Three times a year somebody tries to cross the yard at night and three times a year the dog wins.
bestiary.gallows.lore: An oak beam, two ropes, and a board with names. The executioner hangs people here once a quarter, and the town pays him for the work, not for the result — which is the cause of his only complaint.
bestiary.gap.lore: A breach in the west wall, two ells wide, covered by a board. Idzi claims it does not exist. Bernard claims he knows of it. Rawicz claims it is not in his report.
bestiary.goose.habitat: The pastures behind the mill, the stream bank.
bestiary.goose.lore: The pasture geese belong to the miller, and the miller claims they guard his yard better than a dog. He may be right — geese are louder.
bestiary.harbour.lore: Three piers, two warehouses and a customs house. At dusk the harbour changes owner: by day it belongs to Bernard, by night to Idzi. The guard knows and looks the other way, for a fee.
bestiary.hemlock.lore: It looks like wild parsnip and like young yarrow. Three paces off a path you walk every day. There is no antidote — only time.
bestiary.horse.habitat: The stable by the inn, the road to the north gate.
bestiary.horse.lore: Paweł says a horse knows when the rider is afraid. Five crowns a day is the price of a horse that is not afraid with you.
bestiary.knight.habitat: The house with the black crow, night patrols, the customs gate after dusk.
bestiary.knight.lore: They take a tenth of everything and they have a sealed paper. In 1428 they came into town at the guild's invitation to put down a rising. They did not leave. Nobody asked them to stay.
bestiary.market.lore: Four stalls, a notice board, and a gallows in sight — deliberately, so the price of bread seems fair. A crowd at noon, empty at dusk, a patrol at night.
bestiary.pike.habitat: The stream by the bathhouse, the depths past the east pier.
bestiary.pike.lore: Ewa catches pike with a net, not a hook, and says pike is a fish for people who have time. Everybody else eats sprat.
bestiary.rat.habitat: Warehouses, piers, the bins by the inn. It runs from light and follows the smell of fish.
bestiary.rat.lore: Marta says the rat in warehouse B is the size of a cat and that Idzi feeds it on purpose. Nobody has seen this rat. Everybody talks about it.
bestiary.tannery.lore: Four vats, a stream, and a smell that reaches the square. For three years the guilds have argued where Oles may empty them. The argument lasts because nobody wants to pay for a drain.
bestiary.toadstool.lore: Red with white spots. Pretty and worthless if you want to live. Peasants believe it drives off rats — they lay it by the grain sacks.
bestiary.willow.lore: It grows by water, where the midges and the marsh are. Bark chewed eases pain, brewed it lowers fever. Wiera cuts it in March, before the sap runs.
bestiary.wolf.habitat: The eastern marsh and the woods beyond the walls. It comes down to town at night when the frost lasts longer than a week.
bestiary.wolf.lore: In 1429 wolves came onto the square in broad daylight and took a child. Since that winter the north gate closes at dusk and nobody protests.
bestiary.yarrow.lore: It grows by ditches and field edges. Chewed it staunches blood. Wiera tells it from hemlock by the stem: yarrow's stem is grooved.
bld.customs.sign: Duty and seals — open until dusk
board.debt.a: Whoever has seen Paweł of the stable, owing me forty crowns. Ten crowns for telling me where he is.
board.debt.b: I pay in coin and ask no questions about what I do next. — Mojsze, pawnshop, west alley
board.debt.title: A creditor seeks a debtor
board.delivery.a: Two crates must be carried from warehouse A to the east pier before dusk. Twelve kilos each. Eight crowns paid.
board.delivery.b: Do not ask about the contents. Do not open. Do not take the lamp-lit road.
board.delivery.c: Ask for Idzi in warehouse B after dark. — Bosun Idzi
board.delivery.title: Delivery to the east pier
board.empty: The board is empty. Nobody wants to trust a stranger.
board.escort.a: A merchant seeks somebody armed to walk with his cart to the north gate after dusk. Twenty crowns, half in advance.
board.escort.b: It is not about thieves. It is about the tenth, which he does not want to pay in front of witnesses. — Guild house
board.escort.title: Escort to the north gate
board.labour.a: The tannery needs two men to move hides for one day. Six crowns and a bowl at the end.
board.labour.b: The work stinks and that cannot be hidden. The water is cold. — Oles, tannery
board.labour.title: Work at the vats
board.missing.a: My son went for water at dusk yesterday and did not come back. Fifteen years old, hooded cloak, boots with one lace.
board.missing.b: I have no crowns. I have a loaf a day for whoever brings him back. — The almshouse by the chapel
board.missing.title: A boy from the suburbs is missing
board.pests.a: The guild pays four crowns for every ten tails. The grain crates are gnawed through, and that matters more than tails.
board.pests.b: Do not use fire in the warehouse. Somebody already tried. — Rejne, guild house
board.pests.title: Rats in warehouse A
board.title: Notice board

branch.survival.desc: Wood, marsh, body: food, warmth, wounds and sickness.

ending.end_captive.text: On the thirty-first day there was no trial. There was a house with a black crow over the door, a windowless room, and a ledger in which your name was entered in the left-hand column — where things are written, not people. The debt keeps growing, except now you have no way to pay it, because it is paid in labour. Bernard looked away as they led you past; Rawicz watched carefully, to remember who looks away.
ending.end_crime.text: The debt is paid, but nobody asks where the money came from. Marta knows your steps, Idzi knows your silences, and Bernard knows a face that is in no ledger of his. Rawicz watches you from across the square and does not move — because he knows that if he did, he would end up in a report nobody wants to sign. You slept at night. That is: you slept with a knife at your belt and your back to the wall, but you slept.
ending.end_death.text: An alley, a plank, a stair — the island has many ways to turn a person into a memory. Somebody carried you to the bathhouse or left you by the wall, depending on how much was in your purse and to whom you owed. Kruk added three more days of interest before he learned there was nobody left to collect from. Hanna left a bowl on the table until evening. Marta asked whether anyone is taking your sword.
ending.end_escape.text: The ship left at dawn, just as it did when you arrived. Only this time you stood at the rail and the island grew smaller. The debt stayed on the shore together with the people you promised something to. Kruk will add interest until he dies and write your name on the board that is read aloud at the gate. The sea is wide and nowhere is closer than here. You have a whole life to find out whether that is enough.
ending.end_honest.text: On the thirtieth day Baldwin Kruk counted the coins twice and nodded. The debt closed to the last crown, the receipt signed in Zbylut's office, the guild seal in place. You did not become a hero — you became a man who can be lent money. Hanna gives you a tab without a word, Orlik keeps better coal aside for you, and Vagn says you hold a sword like somebody who wants to live. The island does not reward honesty; it only remembers it.
ending.end_knights.text: The token with the engraved crow weighs little and opens every door you do not want opened. The tenth passes through your hands and some of it stays on them. Vagn stopped speaking to you; Hanna charges you for a bowl as she would a stranger, because you are a stranger — only better dressed. Kruk pats your shoulder and says he always knew. You have a peace that cannot be spent and a debt that cannot be repaid.
ending.end_overthrow.text: It began at the notice board and with one sentence said too loudly by the well. Then the guild, then the almshouse, then a gate nobody closed on orders. The tenth was not abolished by any decree — people simply stopped paying it, all at once, in a single week. Kruk left in the night, and the house with the black crow over the door has a new door now. There is no hero. There are forty people who did the same arithmetic you did.
ending.hardcore: In hardcore, death is the end. The save has been closed.
ending.title: The end

gamble.keepTwo: Keep two of three dice. The sum counts.
gamble.noStake: You lack {gold} crowns for a stake. Words do not play.
gamble.notWelcome: Hanna does not open the table to strangers. You must be introduced.
gamble.rules: The stake lies on the table. Win and you take it. Lose and you sit on, or stand up.
gamble.searched: Someone at the table looks at your purse too long.

gamble.tooEarly: Before noon only dust sits at the table.

interact.drank: You drink the water. It tastes of the river.
interact.gallows: The gallows. Boards darkened by rain and by things worse than rain.
interact.hostile: {what} is not in the mood to talk.
interact.lockpickBroke: The pick snaps in the lock. Someone heard that.
interact.nobody: Nobody is here. The stall is closed.
interact.searchSeen: {who} watches you rummage through other people's things.
interact.stocks: The stocks. A plank polished by the heads of those who were late with a debt.
interact.warmed: You warm yourself at the fire.

inv.slot.head: Head
inv.title: Satchel
item.aleCask.desc: Fourteen kilos of untaxed cask. To Idzi it is goods; to Bernard it is twenty missing entries in a ledger.
item.antidote.desc: A dark liquid that does not undo hemlock — it only buys time. Seventy crowns for a few hours.
item.apple.desc: Small, sour, from the orchards past the north gate. Better than nothing.
item.arrow.desc: Goose-fletched, oak-shafted. Thirteen to a bundle.
item.axeWar.desc: A broad wedge on a long haft. Not for parrying — for finishing.
item.axeWood.desc: A tool that doubles as a weapon. Heavy, slow, but it splits bone and board with equal enthusiasm.
item.bait.desc: Bread crusts and fish guts. It stinks in your pack all day.
item.bandage.desc: Clean linen in strips. It stops blood, it does not stop infection.
item.beer.desc: Dark, thin, lukewarm. Two crowns and a little courage in liquid form.
item.bitterDraught.desc: A dark liquid in a vial. It tastes like graveyard earth and brings a fever down.
item.bone.desc: A wolf's shin. Hard as horn, good for a knife handle and for a fever broth.
item.bookHours.desc: A small prayer book with margins full of somebody's notes. The church would like it back.
item.bow.desc: A yew bow with twenty paces of reach. In town an arrow is evidence, not just a projectile.
item.bread.desc: Four crowns a loaf because the miller plays dice. Heavy, sour, filling for half a day.
item.candle.desc: Tallow, wick, one hour of light. Enough to read one page, if you hurry.
item.cards.desc: A beer-stained deck. Cecylia knows every stain by heart.
item.chainShirt.desc: Thousands of riveted rings. Nine kilos that save your life and ruin your back.
item.cheese.desc: A hard wheel of ewe's milk. It keeps for weeks; the smell keeps for less.
item.cloak.desc: Thick wool, a hood, a bone clasp. In rain it hangs like armour; in cold it earns its price.
item.coal.desc: Black stone that burns long. Without it a smith is only a smith working cold.
item.crateUntaxed.desc: Twelve kilos of a crate that appears in no ledger. It must be carried across the town in the dark.
item.crossbow.desc: A weapon no burgher may carry. Accurate, slow, very illegal.
item.crown.desc: A silver coin with a king's worn profile. The one thing on the island everyone wants.
item.customsSeal.desc: Bernard's brass stamp. With it a cart passes the gate; without it the cart stands for three days.
item.dagger.desc: Short, quick, easy to hide under a cloak. Good in an alley, poor in a field.
item.deedRoom.desc: A room above the stable, yours for a year. Four walls, a roof, and a neighbour who coughs in his sleep.
item.dice.desc: Two knucklebone dice. On one of them the six is worn more often than on the other — check before you bet.
item.egg.desc: Three eggs the size of a fist. In a pan they will feed two people.
item.falsePapers.desc: Someone else's name on good paper. A hundred crowns from Idzi, a rope at the gate if you slip up.
item.feather.desc: Flight feathers for arrows and quills for writing. One feather, two uses, one unhappy goose.
item.fish.desc: Harbour sprat smoked in sawdust. Salty, lasting, and it smells like the whole alley.
item.flint.desc: A scrap of steel and a flint. Without it a torch is only a stick, and night is only night.
item.garlic.desc: Garlic in a braid. Wiera hangs it over the door and says it is against the plague. She may be right.
item.gem.desc: A continental stone set in silver. Rejne will give you half its worth and still be pleased.
item.gooseFat.desc: A jar of fat. The base of every salve and half the taste of every stew.
item.grain.desc: Rye in a sack. Eight kilos, fifteen crowns, and the reason a boy from the suburbs will go to the gallows.
item.hammerSmith.desc: Three pounds of iron on an oak haft. Orlik calls it a tool. You know it is also a weapon.
item.hide.desc: A raw hide, still stiff. Oles will take it gladly, provided it was not dried on stone.
item.hook.desc: A bent nail and horsehair line. Harbour fish are stupid, but not that stupid.
item.ironBar.desc: Drawn from the fire, cooled, ready to work. Five kilos worth twenty-six crowns.
item.ironOre.desc: Stone heavier than it looks. From four pounds of ore Orlik wrings one pound of iron.
item.jerkin.desc: Two deer hides and three days of Oles's work. It keeps out rain and the first blow.
item.kettleHelm.desc: The brim keeps off rain and blows from above. You see less in it, but you live longer.
item.knightToken.desc: A plate with an engraved crow. Worn by those who take a tenth of everything. Worth one hundred twenty crowns, or a rope.
item.lantern.desc: A horn pane and a wick. Dimmer than a torch, but it will not set a barn alight.
item.leather.desc: Soft, smelling of oak and urine. Two of these become a cuirass.
item.leatherVest.desc: Hardened leather over chest and back. Enough for a knife, not for an axe.
item.letter.desc: Wax with the church's mark. Father Teodor writes to Zbylut so the merchant will look on you more kindly.
item.lockpick.desc: Three wire hooks. Old locks give way, new ones do not, and somebody always hears the sound.
item.mapIsland.desc: The whole island on one scroll. The eastern marshes are drawn nearer than they are — the fishermen say so.
item.mapPort: Plan of the harbour and Lower Town
item.mapPort.desc: Forty crowns for a parchment. Goslaw drew it by walking, so it lies honestly.
item.mushroom.desc: A parasol mushroom, or something that looks like one. The difference can be the last one in your life.
item.nails.desc: Crooked, but their own. Carpentry on this island stands on exactly these.
item.net.desc: A woven net two fathoms long. Ewa says nets are not bought, they are knotted — and she is right.
item.notebook.desc: Leather binding, twenty-four leaves. Without it you remember no faces, prices or promises. It can soak, burn, or be stolen.
item.oilcloth.desc: A greased square of cloth. It keeps the notebook dry — if you remember to use it.
item.paddedJack.desc: Layers of linen and flax. Light, forgiving, and it stinks after a week.
item.permitPort.desc: A scrap of paper with Bernard's seal. Without it the customs gate is a wall.
item.permitUpper.desc: Ninety crowns and three questions you would rather not hear. The Upper Town is not for everyone.
item.plank.desc: Oak board, seasoned a year. Good for a shield, a coffin, or a door.
item.poison.desc: Spotted hemlock in a vial. Tasteless, odourless, with no antidote. Only time.
item.poultice.desc: Bruised yarrow in a rag. You lay it on the wound and hope it does not fester.
item.purseBig.desc: Heavy, full, still warm from somebody else's belt. Such purses look for their owner for a week.
item.purseSmall.desc: Someone's purse with a few crowns inside. Best not to remember whose.
item.quill.desc: A goose feather and a pot of iron-gall ink. Without it the notebook is only paper.
item.rag.desc: Cut-up linen. Zofia washes it, the medic uses it for dressings, the seamstress for thread.
item.relic.desc: A gilt box with a bone inside, and four hundred years of somebody's prayer. Three hundred crowns at Idzi's, infinity at the church.
item.ring.desc: A crest worn half away. Someone wore it long; someone else will sell it gladly.
item.rope.desc: Twenty ells of rope. Useful for a ship, a well, and things you did not plan.
item.salt.desc: The island's white gold. With duty it costs twelve crowns; without it, five times that and a rope.
item.salve.desc: Fat, herbs, and something you did not want to know. It works faster than prayer.
item.satchel.desc: A leather bag holding her mother's savings: eleven crowns and a silver clasp.
item.scrap.desc: Scraps from a failed forging. Orlik will take them back at a third of their worth.
item.shield.desc: Boards, leather and an iron boss. Heavy, but it turns a cut into a bruise.
item.skinningKnife.desc: A thin, curved blade. It will take a hide off whole, if the hand does not shake.
item.snare.desc: A wire loop on an animal path. It works while you sleep, and sometimes catches the wrong thing.
item.spear.desc: A long shaft, a narrow head. It keeps people away until somebody steps inside it.
item.splint.desc: Slats and a thong. A splinted leg lets you walk; without it, you lie down.
item.stew.desc: Turnip, fish and bread in one bowl. Six crowns at Hanna's, and the best six crowns in town.
item.swordIron.desc: A plain, well-balanced sword. It cuts mail slower than leather, but it cuts.
item.swordRusted.desc: Your sword from the continent. The edge is toothed with rust, the grip remembers another hand. It can be sharpened.
item.tabChit.desc: A wooden tally notched with thirty crowns owed to the innkeep. Whoever holds the stick holds the truth.
item.torch.desc: A stick, a rag, tar. It burns an hour and a half and dies in rain faster than you think.
item.turnip.desc: A root from the field behind the tannery. Boiled in stew it pretends to be meat.
item.venison.desc: Meat from a forest nobody consulted. Raw it ruins your stomach; roasted it fills you.
item.watch.desc: Brass, with a cracked crystal. Two hundred and forty crowns for certainty about the hour.
item.waterskin.desc: A leather bag for water. Fillable at the well, though harbour water is often bad.
item.whetstone.desc: A river stone and an hour of patience. A rusted sword becomes a sword.
item.willowBark.desc: Chewed it eases pain, brewed it lowers fever. It grows by water, which is where the midges are.
item.wolfPelt.desc: Grey, dense, still warm if you are quick. Oles pays forty-eight crowns for a whole one.
item.wolfskin.desc: Fur with a hood. In the woods you smell like a wolf; in town you smell like someone nobody bothers.
item.wool.desc: Unspun wool from the sheep behind the mill. Everything can be woven from it except money.
item.yarrow.desc: It grows by ditches and field edges. Chewed, it stops bleeding — but it is easily confused with hemlock.
journal.favorOwed: You owe Baldwin a favour. You do not know which.
journal.noNotebook: You have no notebook — you remember only the debts, because those remember themselves.
journal.noneActive: You have nothing written down. Without a notebook little can be remembered.
journal.noneDone: You have seen nothing through to the end yet.
journal.payWhere: You pay Gwidon at the customs gate, or Baldwin in person.
map.acquired: You now have a plan of: {region}.
map.heard: Someone told you about: {what}. You draw it as a dashed line.
map.hintKey: Map scroll — key {key}. The map is an object: it can be lost.
map.noMap: You have no map of this area.
map.tooManyMarkers: Too many marks on one scroll. Erase one.
merchant.baker.flavor: A loaf four crowns. The smell of bread reaches the square before dawn and returns only in the evening.
merchant.black.flavor: Goods in no ledger, prices in no list, and a face in nobody's memory.
merchant.cartographer.flavor: A harbour plan forty crowns, the island two hundred forty. Drawn by walking, so it lies honestly.
merchant.customs.flavor: Salt twelve, grain fifteen, fur forty-eight. The seal costs three crowns.
merchant.fisher.flavor: A net twelve, a hook two. After dusk she does not sell, because she cannot see to whom.
merchant.guild.flavor: Buys honestly, sells dear. Duty, receipts, and the argument over who pays for burnt roofs.
merchant.herbalist.flavor: Herbs, salves, and knowledge you pay for in time, not only in crowns.
merchant.medic.flavor: A dressing ten, stitches eight, a bone twelve. Paid in advance.
merchant.pawn.flavor: The pledge stays, interest grows by the day. Redeem in a month — you lose a third.
merchant.scribe.flavor: A notebook twelve, a quill three. He writes contracts for a percentage of the value.
merchant.smithy.flavor: Coal first, then talk. The hammer strikes from five until dusk and does not stop for rain.
merchant.tanner.flavor: A hide forty-eight, if whole. The smell carries across the square and that is part of the price.
merchant.tavern.flavor: A bowl six, beer two, a room five. A tab only for those who come back.
msg.cantUse: There is no obvious use for: {what}.
msg.noFlint: You have no flint. Without fire a torch is only a stick.
msg.poisonedFood: Something was wrong with that food. Your stomach rebels.
msg.sober: The drink clears from your head. Your head aches.
needs.badWater: The water was bad. In a few hours you will regret it.
needs.bandaged: You dress the wounds. The pain quiets.
needs.boneSet: The bone is set. The pain will stay for weeks.
needs.feverStart: The swamp has taken its toll. You shiver despite the warmth.
needs.infected: The wound festers. Red, warm, smelling wrong.
needs.plagueStart: Fever, chills, spots on the neck. This is no common cold.
needs.rotStart: Handling the corpse has reddened your wounds. Something has set in.
needs.splintNeeded: That needs setting and splinting. Not something you can do alone.
needs.treated: The medic tends to you ({gold} crowns).
note.arrival: The ship sailed at dawn. Baldwin Kruk stood on the shore counting on his fingers. Ten thousand crowns, thirty days. I have nothing but a rusted sword and the address of an inn.
note.blood: The first time I killed a man. Not in a duel — in an alley, because he wanted my purse. Blood on cobbles looks like rust. The guard walked past and did not stop. Somebody saw it; I know, because he looked me in the eye.
note.debt: Kruk says the debt grows by twenty crowns a day. If that is true, in a week I will owe more than I hope to earn. I must check whether he counts honestly.
note.fire: Somebody on the market was shouting that a roof is burning in the Lower Town. The guard closes the gate so people will not run. Hanna says it is the third fire this month and there is no insurance, because the guilds are arguing about who pays.
note.idzi: Bosun Idzi did not shake my hand. He said he works for a man who does not exist, and that if I want to move something that is in no ledger I should come after dusk. He mentioned salt — twelve crowns a sack, if nobody is watching.
note.marta: A girl, maybe fifteen, tried to lift my purse. I caught her by the wrist. She did not cry — she only calculated what she would have earned. She said she knows somebody who needs somebody who can walk quietly.
note.vagn: Old Vagn looked at me a while and said I hold a sword like a peasant holds a pitchfork. Then he showed me where the water bucket is. Teaching costs crowns and time — there are no free lessons.
notes.acquired: You now have a notebook and a quill. K and G are no longer empty.
notes.empty.bestiary: Nothing written yet. Look, listen, and write it down.
notes.empty.items: You have described no item yet.
notes.empty.john: John has written nothing about himself.
notes.empty.places: You have described no place yet.
notes.hint: You noted it in your head, but not on paper.
notes.hint.bestiary: Entries appear when John sees, kills, hears, or asks someone who knows.
notes.hintKey: Notebook — key {key}. Without it these pages do not exist.
notes.noNotebook: You have no notebook. Buy one from Urban the scribe.
notes.noQuill: Without quill and ink you can write nothing.
notes.wet: The notebook is soaked ({pct}%). Some entries have run.
npc.baker.address: The bakery on the square, chimney on the east
npc.baker.desire: Flour at the old price and an oven that does not crack in the frost.
npc.baker.greet1: A loaf four crowns, because the miller plays dice and I play with nobody.
npc.baker.name: Grzegorz the baker
npc.baker.secret: He has been adding ground acorns to the flour since grain grew dear. Nobody has complained, but he knows somebody will.
npc.baldwin.address: A room above the stable, by the inn
npc.baldwin.desire: For the debt to be paid to the last crown, and for nobody to think the Knights joke.
npc.baldwin.greet1: Thirty days, John. I count on my fingers so you can see how much you have left.
npc.baldwin.name: Baldwin Kruk
npc.baldwin.role: Debt collector of the Wild Knights
npc.baldwin.secret: He owes the Knights more than John does. If John does not pay, Baldwin hangs first.
npc.beggar.desire: Boots that do not soak, and a place by the fire in winter.
npc.beggar.greet1: A crown, sir. Or half. Half a crown is a loaf for two days.
npc.beggar.name: Lame Jędrek
npc.beggar.secret: He sees everything that passes the gate and sells it to Rawicz for a bowl of stew once a week.
npc.collector.address: The house with a black crow over the door
npc.collector.desire: Receipts signed by every merchant in town, and quiet from above.
npc.collector.greet1: A tenth. Of everything. In coin or in kind, I am not fussy.
npc.collector.name: Raven's man
npc.collector.secret: He skims a tenth of the tenth he collects. The Knights have not counted so carefully yet.
npc.customs.address: The customs house by the harbour gate
npc.customs.desire: A ledger whose numbers agree, and a year without the Wild Knights on his back.
npc.customs.greet1: Salt twelve, grain fifteen, fur forty-eight. The seal costs three.
npc.customs.name: Bernard of the Customs
npc.customs.secret: Twenty sacks of salt are missing from his ledger this month. He knows, and he waits for somebody else to be blamed.
npc.executioner.address: A house by the gallows, outside the walls
npc.executioner.desire: For his son not to have to take up this trade, and for the town to pay for the work, not only for the result.
npc.executioner.greet1: I do not shake hands. It is not manners, it is custom.
npc.executioner.name: Wawrzyniec the executioner
npc.executioner.secret: He lives in a house the town gave him and pays tax on a house he cannot sell. Nobody buys an executioner's house.
npc.fisher.address: A hut by the east pier
npc.fisher.desire: A calm sea, a whole net, and for the harbour not to stink so much that the fish leave.
npc.fisher.greet1: A net twelve crowns, a hook two. I do not sell fish after dusk, because then I cannot see to whom.
npc.fisher.name: Ewa the fisher
npc.fisher.secret: She has seen Idzi's boat at night three times this month. She tells nobody, because Idzi pays her for silence in fish.
npc.gamblerDay.address: The Rusty Cat, table by the hearth
npc.gamblerDay.desire: A table where nobody shouts, and an evening that ends even.
npc.gamblerDay.greet1: Dice three, cards five. I know every stain in this deck — do not cheat, it wastes your time.
npc.gamblerDay.name: Cecylia Cards
npc.gamblerDay.secret: She counts cards for Marta once a week and gets a fifth of the winnings. She does not call it partnership.
npc.gamblerNight.address: The Rusty Cat, table by the window
npc.gamblerNight.desire: For somebody to lose enough to pay off his own debt to Kruk.
npc.gamblerNight.greet1: At night the stakes are higher and the faces are different. Dice five, cards ten.
npc.gamblerNight.name: Fat Nickel
npc.gamblerNight.secret: One of his dice is weighted on the underside. He did not weight it — he inherited it from a colleague.
npc.goslaw.address: A room above the scribe's office
npc.goslaw.desire: Parchment that survives damp, and a year without rain to finish the eastern marshes.
npc.goslaw.greet1: A harbour plan forty crowns. The island — two hundred forty. I drew it walking, so it lies honestly.
npc.goslaw.name: Goslaw the cartographer
npc.goslaw.secret: The eastern marshes are drawn nearer than they really are — because somebody paid him to draw them that way.
npc.greeting.night: Honest people sleep at this hour.
npc.greeting.stranger: I do not know you. What do you want?
npc.greeting.wanted: The guard is looking for you. Do not stand so close to me.
npc.guard.desire: A shift with no incidents, and a hot bowl at the end of it.
npc.guard.greet1: Move along or stand still. There is no third option.
npc.guard.greet2: After dusk this street is closed. No pass, no way through.
npc.guard.name: Guard
npc.guard.secret: The guards wear heads forged by Orlik that are in no ledger. They know they are illegal and wear them because they are good.
npc.guardAlerted: {who} puts a hand on his weapon.
npc.guardCustoms.name: Customs guard
npc.guardNorth.name: North gate guard
npc.guild.address: The guild house on the square
npc.guild.desire: A duty on continental furs and an end to the smuggling that eats his margin.
npc.guild.greet1: I buy honestly and sell dear. That is not a contradiction, that is a trade.
npc.guild.name: Rejne the merchant
npc.guild.secret: He himself buys untaxed salt from Idzi when the price is right. He calls it flexibility.
npc.hanna.address: The Rusty Cat inn, market square
npc.hanna.desire: A quiet inn, full casks, and for the guilds to stop arguing about who pays to rebuild the burnt roofs.
npc.hanna.greet1: Cold? A bowl is six crowns, a room five. A tally tab is only for regulars.
npc.hanna.greet2: You again. Sit by the hearth, not the window — the window is for those who count other people's money.
npc.hanna.greet3: If there is blood on your sleeve, use the back door. I do not want to explain that to the guard.
npc.hanna.name: Hanna of the Mill
npc.hanna.secret: Her husband died in the fire of 1428. She keeps the notched tallies under the counter — some are six years old and were never paid.
npc.idzi.address: Warehouse B, on the west pier
npc.idzi.desire: A ship that leaves without duty, and a son who will not follow him.
npc.idzi.greet1: I do not know you. Good. I know everybody, and that is bad.
npc.idzi.greet2: After dusk, back door, no torch. If you bring a lantern, there is no conversation.
npc.idzi.name: Bosun Idzi
npc.idzi.secret: Idzi's son serves in Bernard's customs guard. Every crate the father carries in could be the one his son opens.
npc.marta.address: She sleeps in the alley behind the bakery
npc.marta.desire: Eleven crowns in a bag and as many in reserve, so her mother stops coughing in a cold room.
npc.marta.greet1: Do not keep your purse at the back. The back is easiest.
npc.marta.greet2: I will teach you for fifty crowns or for one favour. The favour costs more.
npc.marta.name: Marta
npc.marta.secret: Marta's mother washes linen at the guardhouse and knows the guards' shift rotation. Marta knows this and has not decided what to do with it.
npc.medic.desire: Clean rags, clean water, and for people to come earlier than the third day.
npc.medic.greet1: Dressing ten, stitches eight, a bone twelve. You pay first, because afterwards people run.
npc.medic.name: Barber-surgeon Marcin
npc.medic.secret: He cannot read Latin. He buys ready recipes from Wiera and writes them down as his own.
npc.nun.desire: A full almshouse pantry and fewer children who come alone.
npc.nun.greet1: A pallet in the almshouse for alms. Three days, no more — there is a queue.
npc.nun.name: Sister Agnes
npc.nun.secret: She writes down the names of those who never came back for their things. This year the list has eleven entries.
npc.orlik.address: The smithy on the square, brick chimney
npc.orlik.desire: A forge that does not go out, and an apprentice who will not run off to town for the winter.
npc.orlik.greet1: Coal first. Then we will talk about an edge.
npc.orlik.greet2: Whoever brings scrap gets a third of the price. Whoever brings coal gets the anvil.
npc.orlik.name: Master Orlik
npc.orlik.secret: He forges heads for the Wild Knights and does not enter them in the ledger. He knows Rawicz knows, and both stay silent because both profit.
npc.rawicz.address: The guardhouse by the north gate
npc.rawicz.desire: The gate shut at night, no fires, and for the Knights to stop taking a tenth of his men.
npc.rawicz.greet1: You have a pass or you have a reason. Both in writing.
npc.rawicz.greet2: I saw you yesterday. Or the day before. I remember faces better than names.
npc.rawicz.name: Sergeant Rawicz
npc.rawicz.secret: He takes bribes from Orlik and from Idzi — and reports both to the Knights once a quarter, to keep the balance.
npc.screamed: {who} screams and runs toward the market.
npc.scribe.desire: Ink that does not fade, and for the guilds to pay for the paper on which he writes their disputes.
npc.scribe.greet1: A notebook twelve crowns, a quill three, ink five. I write contracts for a percentage.
npc.scribe.name: Scribe Zbylut
npc.scribe.secret: He writes for both sides of the guild dispute and keeps copies. If the copies came to light, the office would burn.
npc.stableboy.desire: A horse of his own and a room without a draught.
npc.stableboy.greet1: A horse five crowns a day, oats two. I do not sell a horse to someone who cannot hold one.
npc.stableboy.name: Paweł the stableboy
npc.stableboy.secret: He sleeps in the stable because he has no room. Kruk knows and does not charge him rent — yet.
npc.tanner.address: The tannery beyond the west alley
npc.tanner.desire: Water that carries no plague, and an end to the guild argument about where he may empty his vats.
npc.tanner.greet1: A whole hide forty-eight, a holed one twenty. Oak bark by weight.
npc.tanner.name: Oles the tanner
npc.tanner.secret: He empties his vats into the stream at night because the guilds refused him a drain. Three wells downstream have water that smells like him.
npc.teodor.desire: For the reliquary to come back from the harbour to the chapel, and for nobody to die without a priest at the bed.
npc.teodor.greet1: I do not ask what you did. I ask what you intend to do.
npc.teodor.greet2: Confession three crowns. Alms two. Silence free.
npc.teodor.name: Father Teodor
npc.teodor.secret: The reliquary was sold to Idzi by somebody from the abbey, and Teodor knows the name and keeps quiet, because it is his brother.
npc.usurer.address: A shop with a barred window, west alley
npc.usurer.desire: A quiet street and customers who come back.
npc.usurer.greet1: The pledge stays with me, interest counts from the day. Redeem it in a month — you lose a third.
npc.usurer.name: Mojsze the pawnbroker
npc.usurer.secret: He keeps a Wild Knight's signet in his safe — pledged, not redeemed, dated four months ago.
npc.vagn.desire: For somebody to outlive what he teaches. The rest is beer and silence.
npc.vagn.greet1: You stand like a peasant with a pitchfork. Elbows up, hips down, breathe.
npc.vagn.greet2: Three exchanges. Touch me once and I will give you the lesson at half price.
npc.vagn.name: Old Vagn
npc.vagn.secret: In 1428 he held the north gate and left it when an order came from the Knights. Three of his men died after he walked away.
npc.washer.address: Tubs by the stream, near the bathhouse
npc.washer.desire: Soap, warm water, and for nobody to bring her shirts that ought to be burned.
npc.washer.greet1: Washing one crown, blood on a shirt two — because I have to wash it twice.
npc.washer.name: Zofia the washerwoman
npc.washer.secret: She washes the guards' linen and knows which of them sleeps away from home. She does not sell that knowledge — yet.
npc.wiera.address: A hut at the edge of the marshes, past the tannery
npc.wiera.desire: For people to stop dying of things growing thirty paces from their door.
npc.wiera.greet1: Show me your hands. Both. The dirt under your nails says more than your words.
npc.wiera.name: Wiera the herbalist
npc.wiera.role: Herbalist and healer of the marshes
npc.wiera.secret: During the plague of 1429 she treated both sides — knights and peasants. The knights burned her hut; the peasants rebuilt it in one night.
pause.hint: The only menu with no counterpart in the world. {key} returns to the game.
pause.title: Pause
perk.beastLore.desc: A wolf is not a monster to you, just an animal with habits.
perk.bellows.desc: The forge holds heat, so one bar goes further.
perk.brewer.desc: The cask does not sour, and the taste is even from first measure to last.
perk.chirurgeon.desc: You will set a bone and stitch skin where another only watches.
perk.chronicle.desc: 1430 is not a date to you; it is a story you know to the end.
perk.coastPilot.desc: You know the shoals around the island. A ship goes where you want.
perk.coldEye.desc: At cards your face says nothing and the other's says too much.
perk.curing.desc: Meat and fish keep longer and do not poison.
perk.cutpurse.desc: A purse moves from belt to hand without a sound.
perk.diceMemory.desc: You remember what fell and know when a die is loaded.
perk.distiller.desc: Stronger tinctures from the same quantity of herbs.
perk.fieldDressing.desc: A dressing laid quickly and cleanly. The wound heals instead of festering.
perk.greenThumb.desc: Herbs grow back faster and the yield is larger.
perk.heavyHand.desc: Blunt blows break a guard instead of merely battering it.
perk.herbarium.desc: You will not mistake yarrow for hemlock. Not at dawn, not in rain.
perk.hiddenPockets.desc: A thief will search you and not find what matters most.
perk.honestFace.desc: A guard looks at you and sees a merchant, not a vagrant.
perk.joiner.desc: Board meets board on the first try.
perk.literate.desc: You can read and write without error. The notebook truly records.
perk.longBreath.desc: Running and trading blows cost less breath.
perk.merchantsEar.desc: You hear when a price has been invented.
perk.parryMaster.desc: The parry window is wider, and a successful turn leaves the enemy open.
perk.quickDraw.desc: You land the first blow before the other can raise his shield.
perk.readGround.desc: You know who passed and how long ago.
perk.requires: Requires: {skill} level {level}, teacher {who}, {gold} crowns, {days} days of study
perk.riposte.desc: After a good parry your blow lands twice as hard.
perk.saltHand.desc: Rope, sail and current are familiar to you. The bosun says one thing less.
perk.shadowWork.desc: At night your hands are quicker and your eyes sharper.
perk.shieldWall.desc: A block holds longer before it breaks.
perk.smoothLie.desc: A lie sounds true even to the man who knows the truth.
perk.softStep.desc: Sneaking is nearly silent. The dog will smell you anyway.
perk.stillWater.desc: Cold water and fatigue do not take away your hand.
perk.streetEar.desc: Rumours reach you before they ripen.
perk.trueTemper.desc: An edge holds longer and does not chip on hard contact.
perk.wireFingers.desc: A pick breaks less often and a lock opens more quietly.
player.name: John of Vranov
prolog.arrival: The ship pushes off. You are left on the pier with one sword and a debt.
prolog.debt: {gold} crowns of debt, {days} days. From today every day has a price.
quest.coal.hint: Bernard sells coal at the customs house until dusk. Idzi will buy or sell after dark, in warehouse B.
quest.coal.journal: Orlik will not let me to the anvil without coal. Three lumps — enough for one day of forging. Coal is at the harbour with Bernard, or untaxed with Idzi.
quest.coal.note: Coal with duty is twenty-four crowns and a clean ledger. Coal without duty is eighteen crowns and somebody else's secret in my pack.
quest.coal.title: Coal for the smithy
quest.marta.hint: Marta sleeps in the alley behind the bakery and does not come out before ten. Cecylia Cards counts for her once a week.
quest.marta.journal: Marta tries to lift my purse and does not cry when I catch her. She says she will teach me for fifty crowns or for one favour. The favour costs more.
quest.marta.note: Her bag holds eleven crowns and a silver clasp. If I return it I will learn things that are in no ledger. If I keep it, I will learn what kind of man I am — and so will Marta.
quest.marta.s1: Find Marta in the alley behind the bakery
quest.marta.s2: Return her satchel or keep it
quest.marta.s3: Cross the square without drawing attention
quest.marta.s4: Go back to Marta with an answer
quest.marta.title: One favour
quest.prolog.journal: I landed at dawn. Kruk counted out thirty days and ten thousand crowns on his fingers. First steps: know the prices, know the people, do not know trouble.
quest.prolog.note: The debt is real because Kruk has a paper with the Knights' seal. Thirty days. If I do not pay there will be no trial — there will be a tenth taken from my hide.
quest.prolog.s1: Speak to Baldwin Kruk on the pier
quest.prolog.s3: Ask Hanna about a room and a bowl
quest.prolog.title: Day one
quest.salt.hint: At night patrols go in pairs by the square and singly by the pier. The west alley has no lamps. The dog at the tannery barks at anyone who smells of salt.
quest.salt.journal: Salt with duty costs twelve crowns; without duty it is worth five times that to whoever holds it. Idzi says it is the simplest work on the island: a sack, a night, a road with no lamps.
quest.salt.note: A sack of salt weighs eight kilos. If the guard searches me, the sack is evidence, not goods. Bernard knows about the twenty missing sacks and waits to accuse somebody.
quest.salt.s2: Carry a sack of salt across the town
quest.salt.s4: Deliver the salt to Rejne or to Bernard
quest.salt.title: Twelve crowns a sack
quest.tab.journal: Hanna gives a tally to regulars. Thirty crowns in notches on a stick. Whoever holds the stick holds the truth — but Hanna remembers every notch.
quest.tab.note: A tab is a debt without interest but with memory. If I do not pay it, Hanna stops feeding me and the whole street learns why.
quest.tab.s1: Take three bowls of stew on the tab
quest.tab.s2: Pay thirty crowns or find another way
quest.tab.title: Hanna's tally
quest.vagn.journal: Vagn said I hold a sword like a peasant holds a pitchfork. He showed me the dummy and the water bucket. Three exchanges — if I touch him, the lesson is half price.
quest.vagn.note: Learning from Vagn costs crowns and time. There are no free lessons, but there is a dummy that does not hit back.
quest.vagn.s1: Find Vagn in the yard behind the smithy
quest.vagn.s2: Survive three exchanges at the dummy
quest.vagn.title: Three exchanges
req.forgeUnlocked: Orlik has let you to the anvil
req.foundGap: The gap in the wall was found
req.saltRumor: You know where the salt comes from
rumor.abbeyLight: They say there is a light in the abbey ruins at night. Father Teodor says it is shepherds; the shepherds say it is not them.
rumor.crimeSeen: They say somebody saw blood on the cobbles by the tannery. The guard washed it off in the morning, but the stone remembers and people remember better.
rumor.customsMissing: They say twenty sacks of salt walked out of the customs house and that Bernard has been questioning himself for a week.
rumor.execution: They say the executioner has work next week and that the board by the gallows will get a new name on it.
rumor.guardBullied: They say the guard held somebody all night again for no reason. Rawicz calls it order; the town has its own word for it.
rumor.johnBetrayed: They say somebody from the harbour sold somebody to the Knights. Idzi has not spoken in two days, which from him means exactly what you think.
rumor.johnFled: They say somebody ran from the guard down the west alley. Apparently he ran so hard he lost one boot and all his dignity.
rumor.johnHelped: They say the new man helped somebody who had nothing to pay him with. On this island that is rarer than an honest customs officer.
rumor.johnLied: They say the new man lies to your face and has already been caught at it once. Apparently he did not even blush.
rumor.johnOffended: They say the new man insulted somebody at the well, in front of everyone. Here such things are remembered longer than debts.
rumor.johnThreatened: They say the new man from the continent threatens people at the gate. Apparently he has neither a crown on him nor any manners.
rumor.knightsLevy: They say the Knights are raising the tenth to an eighth. Nobody has seen the paper, but everybody has seen their men at the carts.
rumor.martaSatchel: They say somebody took Marta's bag and that since then Marta counts people, not crowns. Better not be on that list.
rumor.plague: They say two houses by the north gate have fever and spots. The priest visits them more often than the medic does.
rumor.shipArrives: They say a ship from the continent has come into the harbour. Prices will drop for a day or two, then Bernard will lift them back.
rumor.wolves: They say the wolves came up to the walls again. Since 1428 nobody keeps the gate open past dusk and nobody argues.
save.hardcoreBlocked: In hardcore there are no manual saves.
service.confessed: Relief. Not the kind you expected, but relief.
set.hardcore: Hardcore: one save, death ends the game
set.note: Settings are stored separately from the save, per browser profile.
sign.title: Sign
skill.alchemy.desc: Tinctures, poisons and draughts. Every vial has a price and an effect.
skill.archery.desc: String, breath, distance. In town an arrow leaves a mark in the wall and in a witness's memory.
skill.axe.desc: A swung blow that breaks guard and haft alike. Slower than a sword, heavier in consequence.
skill.barter.desc: Every word fewer is a crown more.
skill.beasts.desc: You know what it eats, what it fears and when it will run. Dog, horse, wolf, boar.
skill.blunt.desc: Mace, club, staff. It does not cut, but it breaks and stuns — and leaves no blood on the cobbles.
skill.brawl.desc: Fists, elbows, head. When you have no weapon, you have yourself.
skill.brewing.desc: Malt, water, time. An untaxed cask is profit; a spoiled one is loss.
skill.carpentry.desc: Boards, nails, a right angle. A door, a shield, a cask, a coffin.
skill.cooking.desc: From the same pot one dish fills you and another undoes your stomach.
skill.dagger.desc: A short blade in close quarters. Quick, it hides in a sleeve, and it does not stop a horse.
skill.deceit.desc: A lie that sounds like the truth. It costs reputation if somebody checks.
skill.endurance.desc: How long you can run, fight and stay upright.
skill.firstaid.desc: Bandage, splint, clean hands. A dressed wound closes; an undressed one festers.
skill.fishing.desc: Net, hook, patience. The harbour feeds you if you know where to cast.
skill.foraging.desc: You can tell yarrow from hemlock only if you learn to.
skill.gamble.desc: Dice, cards, and a face that says nothing. Winning is not luck, it is arithmetic.
skill.herbalism.desc: What grows, what heals, what kills. Wiera knows it by heart and will not teach for free.
skill.history.desc: 1430 has causes. The abbey, the rising, the fire, and why the gate closes at dusk.
skill.intimidate.desc: Sometimes standing close and saying nothing is enough. Guards remember faces.
skill.lockpick.desc: A lock is a mechanism, not a verdict. But the sound carries down the whole alley.
skill.medicine.desc: Infection, fever, plague. The difference between a dressing and an amputation.
skill.parry.desc: Turning a blow at the last moment. It needs eyes, not strength.
skill.persuade.desc: Words work if you know what the person wants.
skill.pickpocket.desc: Somebody else's purse in your hand. If it fails, the whole square sees your face.
skill.reading.desc: Without it a notebook is only scratches and a customs ledger is a wall of numbers.
skill.sailing.desc: Wind, current, rope. Bosun Idzi does not explain twice.
skill.smithing.desc: Heat, rhythm, quenching. The best hammer cannot fix bad stock.
skill.sneak.desc: Shadow, soft step, breath. A guard with a torch sees further than you think.
skill.spear.desc: Reach a sword does not have. It keeps an enemy a shaft-length away until somebody steps inside the head.
skill.streetwise.desc: Who covers whom, where it is cheap, which alley ends in a wall.
skill.sword.desc: Distance, angle, rhythm. The basic thing you brought from the continent.
skill.tanning.desc: Oak bark, water, and a smell you will not wash off. Oles pays well for a whole hide.
skill.tracking.desc: Mud, a broken twig, blood on stone. The woods speak if you know how to listen.
skills.hintKey: The skill page in the notebook — key {key}.
skills.intro: Skills grow from use, not from points.
skills.teacherRule: Only a living person can teach you a perk. You must go to them, pay, and spend days learning.
sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.warning: Sleeping in a public place can be costly: someone may go through your pockets.
